title: `podman machine ssh` creates a literal file named `NUL` on Windows when ssh resolves to MSYS/Cygwin ssh
body:
**Is this a bug report or feature request?**
Bug

**Environment:**
- Windows 11 (build 26300), x64
- Podman CLI **6.1.4** (a per-user install at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Podman\podman.exe`); also reproduces with 6.1.2
- Machine `podman-machine-default`, **WSL provider**, machine server version **6.1.4**
- Shell: **Git Bash / MSYS2**, where `/usr/bin` precedes `C:\Windows\System32\OpenSSH` on `PATH` (positions 3 and 11), so `which ssh` resolves to `/usr/bin/ssh`

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Open Git Bash and `cd` to any directory (ideally a git checkout with a clean `git status`)
2. Run `podman machine ssh true`
3. `ls -la NUL` -> a real file appears (99 bytes)

**Expected behaviour:**
No file is created; host-key checking is discarded without touching the filesystem.

**Actual behaviour:**
A file literally named `NUL` appears in the current working directory, containing a single `known_hosts` line:

    [localhost]:57009 ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIDjy/hMcj54ninkH5cVprxL+hvbcRAfQOGV4ki34QzWB

**Cause:**
`podman machine ssh` spawns

    ssh -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=NUL -o CheckHostIP=no -o LogLevel=ERROR -i <keyfile> -p <port> root@localhost <cmd>

`NUL` is a Windows *device* name, but the `ssh` it spawns is resolved from `PATH`. Under Git Bash/MSYS2 that is the MSYS `ssh`, which treats `NUL` as a *relative filename* and creates it to hold the discarded host key. With the native Windows OpenSSH client the same option behaves as the device, so this only reproduces when the MSYS client wins the `PATH` race.

**Evidence (A/B):**
- default `PATH` (MSYS `/usr/bin` first): file created, 6/6 runs
- `C:\Windows\System32\OpenSSH` ahead of MSYS on `PATH`: not created, 0/4 runs

**Impact:**
`NUL` is a reserved name on Windows (with CON, PRN, AUX, COM1-9, LPT1-9; `NUL.txt` is also equivalent to `NUL`). Such a file cannot be opened by most tools, cannot be deleted with Explorer/`del`, and if it is ever committed it breaks `git checkout` on Windows. It also lands silently in whatever directory the user happens to be in - a common pattern for tooling that shells out to podman.

**Suggested direction:**
Avoid putting a Windows device name in a filename option. `UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null` is not portable to the native Windows client, so a temp file (or resolving a known-good `ssh` rather than one from `PATH`) would be more robust.

comments.body:
> Avoid putting a Windows device name in a filename option. UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null is not portable to the native Windows client, so a temp file (or resolving a known-good ssh rather than one from PATH) would be more robust.

Windows and msys2/cygwin ssh versions have different `ssh -V` output, so, it is possible to check this before creating the command.

There is one scenario where temp file will fail. It is possible to use ssh binary inside WSL container and the host filesystem will not map correctly under this circumstances.
